articles.headline: Despising the Little Ones (Philadelphia street cars; Judge Thompson's decision; Gray's Ferry Passenger Railway)
articles.summary: Introduced: 'Let our Philadelphians read this telling lesson and take warning...' Text: ...men who are earnest and active in soliciting funds to send missionaries to the heathen, behave towards poor colored people, right in our midst, as if they despised them in their hearts. They exclude them from the ballot-box, shut them out of the public schools, kick them out of the public conveyances... In every other Northern city they are allowed to ride in the public conveyances -- but here they are denied that privilege... The latest decision of one of our courts -- the Supreme -- declares that there is no redress for a colored person forcibly ejected from a passenger car; and the flimsy argument of Judge Thompson seems to bolster up and justify that infamous decision... If the colored woman so brutally ejected by the conductor in this instance had been Judge Thompson's own mother, or wife... would he have deemed $5,000 too heavy a fine to have imposed on the Gray's Ferry Passenger Railway Company for such an outrage...

articles.headline: The Condition of the Colored School in Burlington, N. J.
articles.author: T. G.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: -- The examination of the Colored School in this city, came off on Friday morning, 21st inst. This school, located on Wood street, is under the immediate direction of the Trustees of the Public Schools; it is taught by Miss S. La Ran [VERIFY], whose efforts are untiring... This school occupies a room about 18 or 20 feet square... There are about a hundred and ten or twenty children of color in the city of Burlington; of this number, the Trustees have only made provision for forty... [the brick school-house on Stacy street below Union is for white children]... they ought to be allowed to go to the Stacy street school.

articles.headline: Letter from Washington, D. C. (festivals in churches)
articles.author: William Hill
articles.summary: To the Editor of the Christian Recorder: -- Sir, I would like to inquire about the impropriety of holding festivals in the Churches... articles.headline: Some Suggestions to the Colored Soldiers and Sailors
articles.author: Invincible
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: -- Having read a short article in the Recorder of last week, headed, The Colored Soldiers' and Sailors' Convention... Colored Soldiers' and Sailors be careful to select for your leaders, such persons as will reflect honor upon you, not those self-elected, half priest and half politician... Hagerstown, Md., Dec. 22d 1866.

articles.headline: How We Spent the [Sabbath] in the Old [Year] (Philadelphia Sabbath schools and churches)
articles.author: E. W.
articles.summary: In the morning we went [torn] ... heard Brother Hardy [VERIFY]... At ten o'clock, we visited [torn] which is under the superintendence of Wm. Hanton [VERIFY], who has [torn] about a year. This school is well conducted by our [torn] young friend... We left this school, and went to Ghater's [VERIFY: probably Gloster's] Presbyterian Church, of which Brother Robert Jones is the Superintendent... Brother Jones was kind enough to give us an opportunity to solicit the little ladies and gentlemen to sell tickets for the lecture to be given, at Liberty Hall, on January 9th, 1867, by Rev. H. F. Harris [VERIFY], and the little folks came forth, and took almost one hundred... At 3 o'clock we... took our seat in a pew. But the good and faithful pastor, Rev. J. B. Reeves, saw us... Rev. J. P. Turpin, our young hero, who is to graduate in a few months at the Western Theological Seminary, preached for us... At night we went to Wesley Church, Hurst Street, of which Rev. Wm. M. Watson is pastor. There had been a great rally all day at this church, to raise money to liquidate the claims against it. Rt. Rev. Bishop A. W. Wayman spent the whole day with them... They raised, during the day, we learn, fifty-one dollars.
people: Sabbath school superintendent, Ghater's [Gloster's?] Presbyterian Church (identification with other Robert Joneses not established)

articles.headline: The Holidays
articles.summary: Christmas, the birth day of our Saviour, was, by some, spent in jollification, feasting and mirthful enjoyments... 'Oh, Mr. Brother Weaver, say nothing about that; for Christmas only comes once a year!'... from Christmas until New Year the Philadelphians were indeed amusing themselves by way of attending Fairs and Festivals. The A. M. E. Wesley church, of which Rev. Watson is pastor; the Zion Mission, of which Rev. Gould is pastor; St. Thomas' church, of which Rev. Alston is pastor, and A. M. E. Zion church, of which Rev. Hammer [VERIFY] is pastor, have all had a grand time during the holidays... Well, the holidays are now over, and Brother Lynch has not come home yet, and he has been gone from home nearly three months -- and we are anxiously looking for him...

articles.headline: Editor's Budget (Cincinnati)

articles.summary: Cincinnati, Ohio, Dec. 29th, 1866. Two months away from home and still in Cincinnati! ... Peterson, of New York, Bassett, of Pennsylvania, and Clark, of Ohio, are doing more for the cause of education in their respective States...

articles.author: E. W.
articles.summary: We have received word from Rev. Bishop Payne, President of Wilberforce University, that the new building being erected instead of the one burned, is now opened for the reception of students in the theological department... also that the Medical Department was opened on the first day of this month... they have now four professors.

articles.headline: Colored Soldiers' and Sailors' National Convention (letter on its aims; Spruce and Pine St. car case)
articles.author: Alfred M. Green
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: -- All eyes are turned to the great gathering of the Colored Heroes of the war, which takes place on the 8th and 9th of January coming. There are many reasons why this Convention should thus claim the attention of the public... No amount of effort... could procure a situation for a colored soldier under the auspices of the Soldiers' Messenger and Express Co.... A case of the most shocking brutality occurred on the Spruce and Pine St. line, and was tried in our Supreme Court at its present term. One woman was kicked out of the car, and the other in order that she might be subjected to even greater insult, was prevented from leaving the car by the driver and conductor, and driven to the horse-stable at the terminus of the road. All this was proven by white and colored witnesses... And yet, because it could not be proven that the Company required this brutality... they were turned scott-free... We now propose to take hold of this question and with the aid of our friends, if possible, to peaceably secure our right to be treated as men... Respectfully yours, &c. Alfred M. Green.

articles.headline: Christmas Pastime, or Carpenter's Address to the African Race
articles.author: Henry Doyle Carpenter
articles.summary: It is a melancholy fact, that we are standing in a country that refuses to give us our rights as citizens. I your obedient soldier, have contemplated on writing something in our behalf. Shall we who have fought and bled to save this once distracted country, be told we have no right to become citizens... Massachusetts has nobly taken the lead in sending two black men to the Legislative halls... Yours respectfully, Henry Doyle Carpenter, 1st Sergt. Co. F [VERIFY], 43rd U. S. C. T. Trenton, N. J., Dec. 25th, 1866.

articles.headline: How We Spent the First Sabbath in the New Year
articles.summary: It was pretty pleasant over head, and the sun was shining, but apparently dimly... We attended morning services at Union A. M. E. church, of which Rev. R. P. Gibbs is pastor... Bro. Gibbs informed us that it was a speaking meeting, for special prayer for families... In the afternoon we paid a visit to Wesley Sunday School, and Mr. Hookerson [VERIFY] would have us address the school... We had promised Mr. Jones, of the Presbyterian Sunday School, to be with them on the same day... We also attended worship there, and had the pleasure of hearing Rev. Mr. Reeves... At night we were with Rev. Mr. Hemer [VERIFY], of the A. M. E. Zion church, and heard Friend Harris give a short exhortation...

articles.headline: John W. Price (entertainment for Frederick Douglass)
articles.summary: This gentleman keeps a large restaurant on the corner of 4th and Chestnut Streets, and we, having had so much to attend to, have failed, until now, to speak of what took place at his very magnificent dwelling on Broad Street, on the night Frederick Douglass, Esq., was in the city. And what was that? Why, our very highly esteemed friend and brother, after the lecture, gave an entertainment for Mr. Douglass, and invited about eighty or ninety persons, white and colored, composed of the most refined and cultivated society in our city... we think he has the finest finished residence in his square, -- a credit alike to himself and the city.

articles.headline: The Fair at Cincinnati / The Christian Recorder (Lynch ill at Galena)
articles.summary: The fair at Cincinnati for the purpose of raising moneys to aid in purchasing printing material for the Christian Recorder, closed some days since. Mrs. Charlotte Alexander presented to the editor... the sum of one hundred and forty-two dollars and ninety-two cents. The editor has been lying quite ill at Galena, Ill., but is recovering, and expects in a few days to be in Philadelphia... We will say to our readers, that if the paper fails to be as interesting as usual, it is on account of our having been away, attending the Washington Convention. We thought that Rev. James Lynch would have been home before this time...

articles.headline: Hon. George Thompson (lecture at Liberty Hall)
articles.summary: Hon. George Thompson, of England, delivered one of his fine lectures, on last Monday night, in Liberty Hall. Subject -- 'Triumphs of Freedom! The position and prospects of the colored people in the United States.' It was one of the powerful lectures of the day. We are sorry that the inclemency of the weather prevented a very large number from being present... We think that the lecture ought to be published in pamphlet form.

articles.headline: Revivals in the Churches (Bethel revival)

The Bethel church, of our city, of which Rev James Hollen is pastor, is having quite a revival. A number have professed religion and many have been added to the Church... Brother E. B. Davis... Brother Franklin, of Chillicothe, Ohio...

articles.headline: Astonishing to the World (Conference receipts for the Book Concern)

We give below the amount received from our Conferences... Philadelphia Conference, May, 73.12 [two-cent money]... Semi-Centenary contributions: Philadelphia Conference, 312.86 [VERIFY]... The expenses of the paper per week, on an average, are about $110 -- For a year, $5720... what is the General Book Steward and Editor to live upon? On eight or nine hundred dollars a year?

articles.author: F.

After a lingering illness, borne with Christian patience, thou hast fallen asleep in the arms of Jesus... ... When but a child, the Spirit of the Lord worked upon her heart and at the age of seventeen, she embraced religion... calling her companion and her children to her bed-side... articles.headline: The Washington Convention (National Equal Rights League convention, Washington; Langston admitted to the Supreme Court bar)
articles.author: W. A. M.
articles.summary: The National Convention of colored men called to meet at Washington for Jan. 10th, has been held, and its proceedings are now before the country and the world. The convention was composed of splendid material. No abler convention has ever been held, and none which has brought our cause so prominently before the American people. ... besides the cool and able head of J. Mercer Langston, the President of the convention, there were present Prof. Ebenezer D. Bassett, who did most excellent service as chairman of the Business Committee, Prof. Geo. B. Vashon, the author of the able and scholarly address to the colored people, adopted by the convention, Prof. Wm. Howard Day, Bishop A. W. Wayman, Wm. D. Forten, Rev. Benj. F. Tanner, and others... (Dated Baltimore, Jan. 22d, 1867.)

articles.headline: Outrageous Conduct of a City Car Conductor (Pine street car)
articles.summary: Under 'Philadelphia Affairs': on the evening of Jan. 2?th [day VERIFY] Mr. and Mrs. Robinson and the writer entered Pine street car No. 2? [number VERIFY]. The conductor took Mrs. Robinson's fare, then ordered them out, saying it was against the rules of the company to allow colored people to ride. They refused; a gentleman asked whether any passenger objected and all answered no. About twenty ladies and gentlemen were in the car. The car was lifted from the track, Fifth and Pine streets were barricaded with wagons, carts and carriages, about 150 persons gathered; the conductor opened the doors, hoisted the windows, removed the cushions and put out the lights, but they remained 'like the rock of Gibraltar.' (STREETCAR topic.)

Miller, pastor of the Pearl street Baptist Church, presented petitions to the legislature for the bill, with many signatures. Also p.3/p.2: Miss Jane M. articles.headline: Another Triumph of Liberty (editorial on the Pennsylvania anti-exclusion car bill)

This week we have the great satisfaction of chronicling its passage by the House, and we trust that next week we shall be able to say that Governor Geary has affixed his signature, and made it the Supreme law of the Commonwealth. We have suffered in consequence of the inhuman regulations of these mercenary companies that grid-iron our city... With nothing to aid them but that of the justice of their cause, the colored people of this city, have continually and earnestly protested against the course of these car companies... events.name: Colored Soldiers' and Sailors' (National) Convention, National Hall, Philadelphia -- first day
events.description: The convention of colored soldiers and sailors assembled in National Hall, Market street, on Tuesday the 8th, delegates from Virginia, South Carolina, Louisiana, Maryland, D.C., Kansas, Ohio, Nebraska, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island. Object: formal demand for equality of rights with white soldiers; band performed the national airs. Called to order by A. W. Handy of Maryland; secretary Chas. B. Fisher read the call (Washington, D.C., Oct. 20, '66, Colored Soldiers' and Sailors' League, to meet at Philadelphia Jan 8th '67). Prayer: Rev. Henry J. Garnett [sic, Garnet]. Temporary chairman George M. Arnold, of Louisiana; secretaries George Hart, Johnson Terry and Charles B. Fisher. Committee on Credentials: J. B. Stratton, Pennsylvania; C. M. Fisher, D.C.; A. M. Green, Pennsylvania; R. H. J. Corman, New York; J. H. Jenkins, Rhode Island. Committee on Permanent Organization: James Underdue, Pennsylvania; A. W. Handy, Maryland; D. G. Rider, Pennsylvania; Guy Brinton, Pennsylvania; J. H. Richardson, Pennsylvania; Samuel Jones, Pennsylvania. Addresses by Rev. Mr. Garnett and Col. Hinton (first to recruit colored soldiers), Sergeant A. W. Handy. Permanent officers: President W. D. [printed 'W. It.'] Matthews, of Kansas; Vice Presidents T. H. Hawkins, D.C., J. Underdue, Pa., A. Ward Handy, Md., Chas. Wager, N.Y., J. W. Walker, Ohio, S. F. Robinson, N.J., J. H. Stratton, Pa.; Secretaries J. H. Richardson, Ohio [sic -- Pa. on the committee], G. R. Hart, Pa., G. D. Johnson, D.C. Business Committee: A. M. Green, Pennsylvania; G. M. Arnold, Louisiana; J. Underdue, Pennsylvania; Owen Dawson, Pennsylvania; G. E. Stephens, Pennsylvania; William Still, Pennsylvania. Afternoon: President William D. Matthews; prayer J. M. Logan of New York; secretary George D. Johnson taken ill; Comrade J. B. Stratton read resolutions for the soldiers, sailors and citizens of Pennsylvania; letters from Hon. Richard Yates, Gen. Louis Wagner, Rev. H. H. Garnett, ex-Gov. John A. Andrew, Hon. Geo. W. Julian, E. C. Ingersoll, colored soldiers at Vicksburg. Honorary members (credentials report by Underdue): L. T. Pelham, J. J. Spilman, W. Howard Day, J. W. Logan, Moses H. Cass, of New York; Professor G. B. Vashon, J. C. White, Sr., W. B. [sic] Forten, J. C. Bustill [printed 'Bostill'], Octavius Catto, Rev. J. B. Reeves, of Pennsylvania; R. P. Hill, J. L. Lyons of Virginia; General Louis Wagner, of Philadelphia; H. H. Francisco [VERIFY], Rev. Elisha Weaver, Rev. James Holland [sic; = Bethel's James Hollen?], Rev. Thomas Gibbs, Rev. W. J. Alston, Rev. Theo. D. Miller, J. C. Wars [VERIFY; Wears?], J. R. Hemry [VERIFY], Stephen Colwell, Wm. Nesbit, President E. R. League, Pa. Comrades Green (rules; resolutions No. 2 to Congress), Major, Hinton (memorial to Congress), Stephens, Myres. Evening: addresses by J. W. Loguen, H. H. Garnett, Col. J. Hinton, Wm. Howard Day, John Mercer Langston. Adjourned 11 o'clock.

Robinson of Ohio. Finance committee: Mr. Pulpress [VERIFY] of Pennsylvania chairman, with Yancey (Ind.), Logett (N.C.), Doram (Ky.), Mahony (Ind.). Address to Congress: Dr. S. J. Brown (Md.), R. H. Johns (N.J.). Resolutions on suffrage, Nebraska 'white' constitution, thanks to Congress and the American Missionary Association; Mr. Weaver, publisher of the Christian Recorder, moved an amendment striking the reference to the AMA; Mr. Carson? Pepper, a white lawyer, delegate from an equal suffrage association, addressed the convention. D.C. ward delegates named (non-Phila). Second day: prayer by Bishop A. W. Wayman; League business with J. M. Langston president; committee to amend constitution: Professor Vashon, W. B. Forten [printed 'W. B. Fort?'], Rev. E. Hackett moved the Convention recommend celebration of the 1st of January as Emancipation day. (Officers and closing business from the foot of column 6 and column 7, read in a second pass: E. Weaver of Pennsylvania on the Executive Committee.)

Campbell. Wm. M. Watson, Pastor. Printed as 'A. M. E. Wesley church' without street: defaults to the Little Wesley lane (FLAG).

events.name: Grand Masonic Presentation at Liberty Hall: communion services to Bethel and Central Presbyterian churches
events.description: On Thursday evening Jan. 31st, at Liberty Hall, the M. W. Grand Lodge A. Y. M. for the State of Pennsylvania presented a handsome communion service of plate to Bethel Church, and the Grand Encampment presented one to the Central Presbyterian Church. Audience about 1500. Blue Lodges, Chapters and Encampments assembled and marched to the hall with a band; choirs of Bethel and Central Presbyterian churches sang. Rev. Redman Faucett [VERIFY] made the presentation for the Grand Lodge to Bethel; Rev. James Lynch accepted for the church; addresses by the pastor Rev. James Hollen and Mr. Abraham Fields. Rev. P. D. Miller [VERIFY] presented on behalf of the Grand Encampment to Central church, acknowledged by its pastor Rev. John B. Reeves and Mr. Jones, an elder. Benediction by Rev. W. G. [VERIFY] Cooper. Committee of arrangements (names inscribed on the vessels): Crawford Hardey [VERIFY], Henry H. Gilbert, Charles H. Edwards [VERIFY], W. A. R. Smith [VERIFY], George W. R. Hall [VERIFY], Southern Forten [VERIFY], James T. Robinson [VERIFY], John Dean [VERIFY], chairman. Faint impression; read at DPI 1600 with contrast enhancement. (PARADES/lodge turnout; LIBERTY HALL topic.)

events.name: A Good Time with Bishop Campbell -- birthday visit by A.M.E. ministers
events.location: Bishop Campbell's residence, 1510 [VERIFY] Addison street, Philadelphia
events.description: On Wednesday 6th inst., Bishop J. P. Campbell's birthday (entering his 52nd year), A.M.E. ministers called at his residence on Addison street [number VERIFY]: Revs. William Moore, Stephen Smith [VERIFY], Joshua P. B. Eddy (printed form unclear), Theodore Gould, R. P. Gibbs [VERIFY], George Boyer, William Williams, William Watson, W. W. Grimes, Elisha Weaver, James Lynch, James Hollen, Henry J. Rhodes, Isaiah Pindell [VERIFY], Edward Young, and Bro. Burris (music). The Bishop and his lady gave a collation; Rev. William Moore, 'oldest member of the Philadelphia Conference,' spoke at Lynch's call; Revs. J. P. B. Eddy, Weaver and Lynch also spoke.
attendees: oldest member of the Philadelphia Conference (Rev.)
Rev. (printed 'J. P. B. Eddy' in the speakers line)

events.name: Bethel Church: Bishop Campbell preaches and administers the Lord's Supper
events.description: Last Sabbath at Bethel Church Bishop J. P. Campbell preached; the Lord's Supper was administered, assisted by Elders Hollen, Smith, Watson, Lynch and Williams and Deacons Joshua Eddy, Josiah Eddy, Pierce and Hardy. Afternoon: Rev. William Williams of the Lancaster circuit preached; a clerical gentleman from England present. Night: Rev. Bro. Pierce preached. Same column: Frankford, Rev. Joseph Smith pastor, about 60 souls added, house too small. (Joshua and Josiah Eddy both printed: owner's ruling makes Joshua/Josiah P. B. Eddy one person; here two deacons are listed side by side -- FLAG.)
attendees: deacon (Rev.), assisting at the Lord's Supper; printed 'Joshua Eddy, Josiah Eddy' as two names, one man by Michiko's ruling

events.name: Bishop Campbell's lecture at Liberty Hall announced (for Little Wesley and Zion Mission)
events.description: Editorial item: Bishop Campbell will lecture at Liberty Hall on Wednesday evening Feb. 20th, subject 'Scenes and observations among the Freedmen of the South'; proceeds to aid the Little Wesley and Zion Mission churches.

events.name: Fight for the Flag: Sabbath-school superintendents of the Philadelphia Conference
events.description: Notice to Sabbath-school superintendents of the Philadelphia A.M.E. Conference to report before the Conference convenes in Bethel Church in May [day printed 1?th; Feb 2 p3 notice says May 18th], by order of Bishop Wayman; Clarke's Commentary offered as prize to the superintendent of the most successful school.

events.name: Street-car bill meeting at Scott's Church
events.description: Philadelphia Affairs: on Monday evening last a meeting was held in the basement of Scott's Church by the committee of colored gentlemen working for the passage of the bill securing the right to ride in the street cars; Messrs. Bowser, Catto and Forten spoke and money was raised; Messrs. De Large (of South Carolina) and Harris (of North Carolina) also spoke. (STREETCAR topic; the Equal Rights League railroads committee -- D. B. Bowser, O. V. Catto, W. D. Forten -- by surname only, so not linked.)

events.name: Benevolent Daughters of Wesley Society -- 45th anniversary
events.location: Philadelphia (Wesley church; which Wesley not stated)
events.description: 45th anniversary of the Benevolent Daughters of Wesley Society, Wednesday evening Feb. 13th: history read by Mr. John H. Hughes; addresses by Revs. James Lynch and Stephen Smith. Plain 'Wesley' -- default Little Wesley lane, FLAG.

events.name: Rev. W. H. Day lectures at Wesley Church, Lombard street
events.description: Rev. W. H. Day lectured at Wesley Church, Lombard street, Tuesday evening last, then returned to Washington; he has been ordained in the A. M. E. Zion connection (p1: licensed by Supt. Clinton). Lombard Street Wesley = BIG WESLEY (A.M.E. Zion).

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church revival; Bishop Campbell baptizes 15 adults
events.description: Union A.M.E. church, Rev. R. P. Gibbs pastor, in great revival, 54 joined. Last Sabbath the pastor preached in the morning; in the afternoon 15 adults were baptized by Bishop Campbell and the Lord's Supper administered; Rev. T. D. Miller of Pearl Street Baptist preached at night. Church crowded.

events.name: Rev. James Lynch to preach sacramental discourse at the Zion Mission Church
events.location: Zion Mission Church, Seventh below Dickerson street, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: Rev. James Lynch, editor, will preach the sacramental discourse at the Zion Mission Church, 7th below Dickerson street, tomorrow (Sunday) afternoon; signed by the pastor, '[Theo.?] Gould, Pastor' [signature blurred, VERIFY].

events.name: Rev. Elisha Weaver to preach at Bethel church on the Priesthood of Melchisedec
events.description: Notice: On Sunday night at Bethel church a sermon will be preached by the Rev. Elisha Weaver, subject 'The Priesthood after the order of Melchisedec...'; young men especially invited.

events.name: M. W. Grand Lodge F. & A. Ancient York Masons of New Jersey -- annual communication and installation (Burlington)
events.description: Notice dated Feb 7, signed O. L. Davis, R. W. G. Sec.: at the annual communication at Burlington, N.J., Dec. 27, 1866, installed: Dempsey Butler [VERIFY], M. W. G. M.; William H. Longfellow [VERIFY], R. W. D. G. M.; A. H. Hi[?] [VERIFY], R. W. G. S. W.; C. N. Robinson, R. W. G. J. W.; Henry Mackey [VERIFY], R. W. G. T.; Obadiah L. Davis, R. W. G. S. Appointed: Rev. Brethren E. Mann [VERIFY], Joseph Francis, W. H. Pitts [VERIFY], Grand Chaplains; Isaac Wells; C. T. Gardiner [VERIFY]; John Huggs [VERIFY]; Daniel Cuff; Henry Carter; Nathaniel Lane; Perry Wilson; J. T. Derrickson [VERIFY]; Freeman Gould. District D.G.M.s: H. H. Williams (Cape May, Atlantic, Cumberland, Salem); C. T. Colwell [VERIFY] (Gloucester, Camden); Charles Williams (Burlington, Mercer, Ocean); J. M. Lowry (Monmouth, Middlesex, Somerset); Joshua Woodlin (Essex, Hudson, Morris, Passaic); Joseph Garrison (Bergen, Hunterdon, Warren, Sussex). Committees: Landmarks O. L. Davis, H. H. Williams, F. Gould, H. Mackey, J. Dolphin, J. H. Benn [VERIFY]; By-Laws J. Woodlin, O. L. Davis, M. Harmon; Charity J. Dolphin, J. A. H. Groves, M. Smith; Correspondence J. H. Benn, C. N. Robinson, H. Mackey. N.J. lodge (Philadelphia Conference territory); roster kept in text only per the common-name/N.J. rule -- the possible William H. Longfellow (the Philadelphia dentist?) is an identity question for the owner.

events.name: Daughters of Wesley -- 45th anniversary (fuller report)
events.description: 'Anniversary of the Daughters of Wesley': the 45th anniversary was held on Wednesday evening February 13th. Officers: Mrs. Mary Frisby (printed 'Mery'), President; Mrs. Elizabeth Johns [VERIFY], Vice President; Miss [given name illegible] Holland [VERIFY], Treasurer; John H. Hughes, Secretary. The President presided; the Secretary read an encouraging report: the funds have not been closed in 45 years; old members too poor to pay dues have them paid; a dividend every five years; about $1000 in bank. Addresses by Revs. James Lynch and Stephen Smith; refreshments. (Same event as the Feb 16 brief notice of the 'Benevolent Daughters of Wesley Society'. Plain 'Wesley' -- FLAG.)

events.name: Lincoln Literary Association -- Lincoln's birthday entertainment at Liberty Hall
events.description: The Lincoln Literary Association celebrated the birthday of our lamented President on Tuesday the 12th inst. by a social entertainment at Liberty Hall. Regular toasts: 'The day we celebrate,' Mr. Luke Wiot [VERIFY]; 'The Memory of Abraham Lincoln,' Mr. Allen Lewis (printed 'Alleo'); 'The United States of America,' Mr. Benjamin Harrad [VERIFY]; 'The Thirty-ninth Congress,' Mr. E. Diggs [VERIFY initial]; 'The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania,' Mr. J. C. Waterford [VERIFY initials]; 'The City of Philadelphia,' Mr. Robert Bryan; 'Woman, the source of all our joys,' Mr. Henry Anderson. Volunteer toasts followed. (LIBERTY HALL topic.)
attendees: toast, Memory of Abraham Lincoln (printed 'Alleo Lewis')

events.name: Hon. Hugh L. Bond lectures before the S. C. S. Association at National Hall
events.description: Judge Hugh L. Bond of Baltimore lectured in this city before the S. C. S. Association (Social, Civil and Statistical Association) at National Hall on Thursday evening the 14th inst., on the condition, prospects and progress of the colored people of Maryland. Same page: Major General O. O. Howard to give the 7th lecture of the S.C.S.A. course on Thursday evening Feb. 28 at National Hall, Market street above 12th; admission 25 cents.

events.name: Rev. James Lynch to preach to the young at Central Presbyterian Church
events.location: Central Presbyterian Church, Lombard street above 9th, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: Rev. James Lynch will preach the first of a series of sermons to the 'Young' at the Central Presbyterian Church, Lombard street above 9th, on Sunday evening (tomorrow) at 7 1/2 o'clock. J. B. Reeves, Pastor. Same column: the Philadelphia Zion Mission Church, long languishing, now healthy under 'brother Gould, the pastor', Sabbath-school flourishing; Mount Holly, N.J., two-week revival under Rev. Jacob Mitchell of the Burlington circuit (52 professed, 40 joined), Rev. Jacob Jay assisting; colored free school taught by Miss Carrie Highgate.

events.name: A. G. U. O. B. A. S. Moses -- First Quarterly Grand Communication (Benezet Hall)
events.location: Benezet Hall, South Seventh street below Lombard, Philadelphia
events.description: Paid notice: the First Quarterly Grand Communication of the A. G. U. O. B. A. S. Moses [Ancient (Grand) United Order of Brothers and Sisters of Moses] met at their hall (Benezet), South Seventh street below Lombard, Tuesday February 5, 1867. Opened with singing and prayer by Rev. J. P. Hamer [VERIFY]. Officers present: H. D. F. Pyle [VERIFY], A. G. W. S.; Anna G. Scott, A. G. W. V. S.; Chas. Emory, D. W. S.; Hannah Emory, D. W. V. S.; Jas. H. D. Carpenter [VERIFY], P. G. W. S.; Emeline Nicholas, P. G. W. V. S.; Alex. T. Bowman [VERIFY], R. S.; Margaret D. Lewis, R. S.; Araminta Hodges [VERIFY], T.; Sarah E. Wood, C.; Jas. H. Hill, D. S.; Chas. Hunter, I. S.; Geo. A. Scott, D. M.; J. P. Hamer, G. C. pro tem. Afternoon: Chas. Emory in the chair, assisted by Anna G. Scott. Jas. H. D. Carpenter appointed Corresponding Secretary; Elizabeth [Highgate?] [VERIFY], P. G. W. V. S.; Rev. J. P. Hamer, G. H. M. [VERIFY]. Three Tabernacles from the Grand Tabernacle Mount of God No. 1 (proof cited to a Miscellaneous Book, county of Phila., Dec 19, 186?): No. 1 Mount Sinai Tabernacle (organized at the Philadelphia Institute, reorganized Nov. 1866?), meets 1st and 3d Monday, Chas. [?] Murray, W. S.; No. 2 Mount Horeb Tabernacle (organized Nov. 1866?), removed to Benezet Hall, meets 2d and 4th Monday, J. H. D. Carpenter, W. S.; No. 3 Mount [El Sur?] Tabernacle, organized Nov. 1866?, located in the rear of the A. M. E. Macedonia church, Spruce St., [South] Camden, N.J., meets 1st and 3d Tuesday, Chas. Emory, W. S. (SOCIETY MEETINGS topic.)
attendees: D. W. S.; chair (afternoon); W. S., No. 3 Tabernacle

events.name: Philadelphia Common Council -- resolution recommending the Sunday Car bill and that colored persons be permitted to ride
events.description: STREETCAR topic. Reported in News of the Week (City), issue of March 2, 1867: 'A resolution recommending the passage of the Sunday Car bill now before the Legislature, and that colored persons be permitted to ride, has been adopted in Common Council.' Date of the vote not stated (late February 1867). The adjacent 'Pennsylvania' legislative paragraph is illegible on the film.

events.name: Preaching services at Wesley A. M. E. Church, Hurst Street (Little Wesley)
events.location: Wesley A. M. E. Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Afternoon, 3 o'clock: Rev. J. W. Bonowell [VERIFY] to preach. Evening, 7 1/2 o'clock: Rev. James Lynch (the Recorder's editor, back in Philadelphia) to preach. Notice signed Wm. M. Watson, Pastor.

events.name: Pennsylvania House of Representatives passes the Sunday car bill (yeas 46, nays 38)
events.description: STREETCAR topic. CR Mar 9 1867 p3, News of the Week, Pennsylvania: 'On the 2[6th or 8th; February] the House of Representatives passed the bill authorizing the Citizens' Association to take charge of inebriates, also the Sunday car bill, (yeas 46, nays 38.) Mr. Wallace was the only Philadelphian voting against it. The result was greeted with applause.' Context: Common Council's resolution (CR Mar 2 p3) recommended the Sunday Car bill AND that colored persons be permitted to ride. This item does not say whether the passed bill touched colored passengers.

events.name: Ejection of Mrs. Sarah G. Thompson from a city railroad car; conductor arrested
events.location: Philadelphia (city railroad car; complaint before the Mayor)
events.description: STREETCAR topic. 'One day last week' (early March 1867): Mrs. Sarah G. Thompson of Princeton, N. J., was pushed from a city railroad car by the Conductor while attempting to get on. She made complaint before the Mayor; a warrant was issued; the Conductor was arrested and bound over in the sum of $600 [VERIFY: 500 or 600] to answer.

events.name: Bethel A. M. E. Church laymen's meeting on union with the A. M. E. Zion Church
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church, Sixth street, Philadelphia
events.description: Held 'last Thursday evening a week' before the Mar 9 issue (computed Feb 28, 1867). Laymen of Bethel considered uniting with the A. M. E. Zion Church; the decision was almost unanimous against union on the terms of 'The Platform of Consolidation.' No officers named.

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association -- lecture by Maj. Gen. O. O. Howard
events.description: 'Thursday evening of last week' (computed Feb 28, 1867). Gen. Howard (Freedmen's Bureau) lectured under SCSA auspices on the condition of the Freedmen to a large audience of both colors. No SCSA officers named.

events.name: U. B. C. concert at National Hall
events.description: 'The Concert given under the auspices of the U. B. C. of this city, at National Hall, on last Tuesday evening, was a grand success in having a large attendance, and giving general satisfaction.' Computed Tuesday Mar 5, 1867. 'U. B. C.' not expanded in the paper (perhaps the Union Beneficial/Benevolent Club; unidentified).

events.name: Banneker Institute lecture: Miss Fanny M. Jackson, 'Industry and Economy, the Guardians of Individual and National Wealth' (LIBERTY HALL)
events.location: Liberty Hall, Lombard Street below Eighth, Philadelphia
events.description: Under the auspices of the Banneker Institute. Tickets 25 cents, sold at 713 Lombard Street by members of the Institute and at the door. Doors 7 o'clock, lecture 8 o'clock. The p2 editorial 'A Good Movement' calls her 'the female Principal of the Institute for Colored Youth' and says the Banneker Institute 'comprises a large number of the most intelligent and prominent young gentlemen of this city.'
attendees: lecturer (Miss), Female Principal of the ICY

events.name: Consecration of the A. M. E. Church of Germantown
events.location: A. M. E. Church, Germantown, Pa.
events.description: 10 1/2 A.M.: Rev. J. Hollen; 3 P.M.: Rev. Bishop A. W. Weyman [= Wayman]; 7 1/2 P.M.: Rev. G. E. Boyer. Invitation to ministers local and itinerant. Signed H. J. Rhodes, Minister in Charge. Page 2 says Rev. Henry J. Rhodes's circuit takes in Norristown, Germantown and West Philadelphia, and that a Germantown church 'is shortly to be dedicated.'

events.name: Post 27, Grand Army of the Republic -- members' meeting
events.description: Members of Post 27, G.A.R. requested to meet Tuesday evening next, 'March 25th' as printed (Mar 25, 1867 was a Monday; 'Tuesday next' from Mar 9 would be Mar 12), at 8 o'clock; all officers to be present. Signed Isaiah M[eyhugh], Post Adjutant (full name clear on Mar 30: 'Isaiah Meyhugh'). RETURNING SOLDIERS topic. Black membership of this post not stated; printed in the CR.

events.name: Sheba Lodge, Juvenile I. O. of Good Samaritans and D. of Samaria -- monthly meetings
events.location: Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Standing notice (dated Feb. 23-1 yr): meets the 2d Thursday of each month at 3 or 8 [VERIFY] o'clock P.M. Officers printed: A. Cropper, P. G.; S. Young, P. G. Full name printed on Mar 30 p4: 'Juvenile I. O. of Good Samaritans and D. of Samaria' (the Mar 9 printing reads 'Juvenile I. O. and D. of Samaria'). The hour prints like 3 on Mar 16, 23 and 30.

events.name: Elisha Weaver's North Carolina tour for the Book Concern
events.location: Norfolk and Portsmouth, Va.; Franklinton, Raleigh, Chapel Hill, Goldsborough, Pittsborough, Haywood, Fayetteville and Wilmington, N. C.
events.description: MIGRATIONS/travel. Weaver's itinerary: Norfolk and Portsmouth Mar 7 (over the Sabbath); Franklinton Mar 13; Raleigh Mar 14-18; Fayetteville Sunday Mar 25; Wilmington, N. C., for the Conference meeting Mar 31. Purpose: subscribers, debts, hymn books. Weaver is in the South from early March.

events.name: Pennsylvania House adopts first section of the streetcar bill (colored passengers' right to ride)
events.description: STREETCAR topic. Editorial 'Riding in the Street Cars' (CR Mar 16 1867 p2): 'last Wednesday' (computed Mar 13, 1867) the previous question was sustained and the first section of the bill adopted, despite Democratic filibustering; the editor calls the right of colored persons to ride in the city's street cars 'guaranteed by the Legislature' and expects the whole bill to pass. Compare CR Mar 9 (House passed the Sunday car bill, 46-38) and CR Mar 2 (Common Council resolution).

events.name: J. Madison Bell reads his original poems at Liberty Hall (LIBERTY HALL)
events.description: 'Thursday night of last week' before Mar 16 (computed Mar 7, 1867): J. Madison Bell gave a reading of his original poems at Liberty Hall. No sponsoring body or officers named. Bell is not a Philadelphian, so he is in the text only, not linked.

events.name: Special all-day services at Wesley A. M. E. Zion Church (Big Wesley)
events.location: Wesley A. M. E. Zion Church, Lombard Street below Sixth, Philadelphia
events.description: 10 1/2 A.M.: James W. Randolph; 3 P.M.: Rev. W. D. F. Pils [VERIFY]; 7 1/2 P.M.: the pastor, Rev. J. P. Hemer [VERIFY]. A collection to aid Rev. J. D. Brooke [VERIFY].

events.name: Rev. James Lynch leaves Philadelphia to visit the Baltimore and southern conferences
events.description: EDITOR/MIGRATIONS. 'The editor left Philadelphia on Friday night of last week for Baltimore' (computed Mar 8, 1867) to visit the conferences; Rev. Elisha Weaver stays in North Carolina until the South Carolina Conference adjourns. With both away, the masthead lines are unchanged ('Rev. Elisha Weaver, Publisher'; 'Rev. James Lynch, Editor').

events.name: Pennsylvania Legislature passes the bill to prevent exclusion from railroad cars on account of color (House passage; awaiting Gov. Geary)
events.description: STREETCAR topic, the culminating item of the quarter. CR Mar 23 1867 p2 editorial 'Another Triumph of Liberty': the State Senate had earlier passed (solid Republican vote, one exception) 'the bill to prevent the exclusion of persons from railroad cars, public conveyances, or any seats therein, on account of their color'; 'this week' the House passed it; the paper awaits Governor Geary's signature. The editorial recalls the colored people's protests against 'the railroad companies of this city' and the Legislature's ignoring of their remonstrance; names Cowan, Buckalew and Simon Cameron (U.S. Senate, context only). CR Mar 23 p3 News of the Week: 'The colored Passenger bill has been passed by both branches of the Legislature'; also 'They agreed to consider the Sunday Car bill at a special session on Tuesday.' Governor's signature not yet reported in my issues (Mar 30 has only pp. 3-4).

events.name: Lecture on the Freedmen of the Southwestern States at the A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street (Little Wesley)
events.location: A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Wednesday evening, March 2[7], 1867 (Wednesday = the 27th). Lecturer 'Rev. [illegible]'; subject '[...] and Observations among the Freedmen of the Southwestern States'. Doors 7 1/2, lecture 8. Refreshment table kept by the Ladies. Notice signed W. M. Watson, Pastor.

events.name: Consecration of the A. M. E. Church, Germantown (postponed from March 17)
events.location: A. M. E. Church, Germantown, Pa.
events.description: Postponed from Mar 17 because of inclement weather; rescheduled for Mar 24, 1867, at 3 P.M., with a sermon by Bishop J. P. Campbell. Notice signed H. J. Rhodes, Minister in charge. (The Mar 9/16 notice had named Hollen, Wayman and Boyer for Mar 17.)

events.name: Bishop A. W. Wayman to preach at Bethel Church, Philadelphia, and tour the Philadelphia Conference circuits
events.location: Bethel church, Philadelphia; then Attleborough, Buckingham Mountain, Burlington N.J., Thornbury, Unionville, West Chester, Coatesville, Lancaster, Marietta
events.description: From 'Bishop Wayman's Appointments' (CR Mar 23 p2): Sunday Mar 31 Bethel church, Philadelphia; Apr 1 Attleborough; Apr 2 Buckingham Mountain; Apr 3 Burlington, N. J.; Apr 4 Thornbury; Apr 5 Unionville; Apr 7 West Chester; Apr 8 Coatesville; Apr 9 Lancaster; Apr 10 Marietta.

events.name: Governor Geary signs the Pennsylvania act prohibiting exclusion of colored persons from public conveyances; Sunday Car bill defeated 12-14
events.description: STREETCAR topic, the outcome. CR Mar 30 1867 p3, News of the Week, Pennsylvania: 'Gov. Geary has signed the bill prohibiting the exclusion of colored persons from the public conveyances.' Same paragraph: 'The Sunday Car bill was defeated--12 to 14'; the Legislature adjourns April 11. Signing date not given (between Mar 23 and Mar 30, 1867, from these reports). Sequence in my issues: Mar 2 Common Council resolution; Mar 9 House passes the Sunday car bill 46-38; Mar 16 editorial on the first section adopted (Mar 13); Mar 23 'Another Triumph of Liberty' (passed both houses) and 'colored Passenger bill has been passed by both branches'; Mar 30 Governor's signature.

events.name: Bethel Church 'Grand Rally' collection for a parsonage
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: 'A Collection to procure a Parsonage for Bethel Church, will be made on Sunday next [Mar 31, 1867]. Let the people rally.' No officers named.

events.name: Revival meetings at Zion's Mission A. M. E. Church; Bishop J. P. Campbell to preach
events.location: Zion's Mission A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: A series of revival meetings in progress, with six or eight professions in the past week. Bishop J. P. Campbell to preach Sunday Mar 31 at 3 P.M.; the meetings continue through the following week. Pastor not named ('little Zion'). Per the brief, the Zion Mission is at Seventh below Dickerson.

events.name: Grand Army of the Republic Post No. 27 -- stated muster
events.location: Benezet Hall, Seventh street below Lombard, Philadelphia
events.description: RETURNING SOLDIERS topic. A stated muster of Post No. 27, G.A.R., Tuesday evening, April 2, 1867; 'important business requires the punctual attendance of each comrade.' Officers: Comrade George E. Stephens, Post Commander; Comrade Isaiah Meyhugh, Post Adjutant. (The same post met at 615 Barclay St. per CR Mar 9.)

events.name: Grand rally at the A. M. E. Macedonia Church, Camden, N. J.
events.location: A. M. E. Macedonia Church, Camden, N. J.
events.description: First Sunday in April 1867 (Apr 7): a rally to raise money toward a deficiency in the pastor's salary. Signed Rev. G. E. Boyer [VERIFY; prints 'Bovan'], Pastor in charge.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church, 1867 session announced
events.description: From 'Meetings of the Conferences of the A. M. E. Church' (CR Mar 30 p3, 4t): 'Philada. Conference, Philadelphia, May 18th, Bishop Wayman.' No church or committees named here.

events.name: Quarterly meetings, Chester circuit and Burlington Circuit
events.location: Chester, Horntown and Chichester, Pa.; Mt. Holly, Evesham and Burlington, N. J.
events.description: Chester Apr 6-7, Horntown Apr 13-14, Chichester Apr 20-21, 1867 (Jeremiah Young, Minister). Burlington Circuit Quarterly Conference at Mt. Holly, Sat Apr 6; quarterly meeting at Evesham, Sun Apr 14; at Burlington, Sun Apr 21.
